questions.question: Which direction should we work out in more detail for ID-268?

options.label: Post-merge snapshot (A) (Recommended)
options.description: Merge is the convergence signal. Trace keeps pr: N; a merged-event workflow posts the block as a PR comment. Needs an RFC-0015 D4 amendment; no token, CI or merge-candidate coupling.

options.label: Cheap close commit (D)
options.description: Keep D4 as is. Agent pushes the block in the same turn, CI path-filters trace-only commits, add a block-presence check. The round trip remains but costs seconds.

options.label: Bot finalizer (shape 1/2)
options.description: Perplexity's conventional answer: a label triggers a bot that commits the block via an App token, then auto-merge. Pays for every constraint; best folded into ID-266's merge-candidate.

options.label: Compare A vs D side by side
options.description: Write both into the dossier as the two remaining options, each with its costs, and settle it alongside BK-384.

questions.question: What should happen to the brainstorm results?
How should the 'final review-round count, computed post-merge' idea land in the ID-268 dossier?

options.label: Fold into shape 6 (Recommended)
options.description: State explicitly that shape 6's purpose includes the final round count (submissions and review-driven commits), and that its post-merge run also counts conversation-comment rounds (issues/<N>/comments). Replaces the 'needs its own item' line; shape 6 grows in scope.

options.label: Make it explicit, keep undercount separate
options.description: Add one sentence that shape 6 yields the final round count, but leave the conversation-comment undercount to its own new backlog item (mint an ID now).

options.label: Own shape, independent of the block
options.description: Add it as shape 10: a post-merge script only counts final rounds (no full block), usable alongside any of shapes 1-9. Smallest piece, decouples the metric from the close-step question.
